definitions.explanation: The area or position closer to the speaker, as opposed to the back or far side.
A point shortly before arriving at a destination.

examples.japanese: {手前|てまえ}のドアから{入|はい}ってください。
examples.english: Please enter through the door on this side.

examples.japanese: {本棚|ほんだな}の{手前|てまえ}に{椅子|いす}があります。
examples.english: There's a chair in front of the bookshelf.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}の{手前|てまえ}で{曲|ま}がる。
{目的地|もくてきち}の{手前|てまえ}で{車|くるま}を{止|と}めた。
examples.english: I stopped the car just before the destination.

examples.japanese: {交差点|こうさてん}の{手前|てまえ}にコンビニがあるので、そこを{右|みぎ}に{曲|ま}がってください。
examples.english: There's a convenience store just before the intersection, so turn right there.

notes: {手前|てまえ} is the opposite of {奥|おく} (back/interior). It indicates the side closer to the speaker. When giving directions, [place]の{手前|てまえ} means 'just before [place].' The word can also be used as a humble form of 'I' in very formal situations, but this usage is quite old-fashioned.
